screens.title: Section C: probability
screens.prose: Section C: 6 questions, four options, +1 right and 0 wrong. Target: about 2 minutes each, 12 minutes. Write the sample space first, simplify, then match. Restart your watch.
screens.question: Type the letter for Q1 to Q6.

rows: **Q1:** Two cards from a 52-card deck. P(same suit)?   **A** 1/4 · **B** 13/17 · **C** 1/17 · **D** 4/17
**Q3:** Flip a fair coin 5 times. P(exactly 3 heads)?   **A** 3/5 · **B** 11/16 · **C** 1/32 · **D** 5/16
**Q4:** Roll a fair 4-sided die; on a 4, roll once more and add. Expected total?   **A** 2.75 · **B** 3.125 · **C** 2.5 · **D** 5
**Q5:** 10% of traders have an edge. A screen flags 90% of them and 10% of the rest. P(edge | flagged)?   **A** 9/10 · **B** 9/100 · **C** 1/2 · **D** 1/10
**Q6:** Roll a fair die twice. P(at least one six)?   **A** 11/36 · **B** 25/36 · **C** 1/3 · **D** 1/36

hints.text: Grid, crowd or tree first; fractions in lowest terms.
Q5: of 1,000 traders, 100 have an edge, 90 flagged; 900 do not, 90 flagged.
Letters: D, B, D, B, C, A.

feedback.correct: All six. Note your time against 12 minutes.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Redo the amber rows from the sample space.

byKey.r0c1: Q1: the second card matches the first’s suit 12 times in 51: $\tfrac{12}{51} = \tfrac{4}{17}$, D. A is with replacement; B is the complement; C is one named suit only.
byKey.r1c1: Q2: four cells of 36 total 5: $\tfrac{4}{36} = \tfrac19$, B. A is the count doubled; C is every total treated as equally likely; D is the complement.
byKey.r2c1: Q3: $\binom53 = 10$ orders of 32: $\tfrac{10}{32} = \tfrac{5}{16}$, D. A is heads over flips; B is the complement; C is one order only.
byKey.r3c1: Q4: $2.5 + \tfrac14 \times 2.5 = 3.125$, B. A is the chance added, not a mean; C is the reroll ignored; D is a reroll every time.
byKey.r4c1: Q5: of 1,000, 90 with an edge are flagged and 90 without: $\tfrac12$, C. A is the hit rate; B is out of everyone; D is the base rate.
byKey.r5c1: Q6: $1 - \tfrac{25}{36} = \tfrac{11}{36}$, A. B is the complement; C is $n \times p$; D is every roll a six.

explain.text: Each wrong option was a classic slip: with replacement, the complement, one order only, or the reverse conditional. Writing the sample space first rules most of them out. The review comes next.
